作者: Bo Qu,Zhurong Wang,Frank Zahradnik,Ming Ouyang
机构: eBay(易贝)
类目: Machine Learning (cs.LG); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL)
备注: 12 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Extends Qu et al., ACL 2025 Industry Track: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Production fraud-detection models learn from a censored slice of their own traffic: transactions a legacy system blocked never receive fraud labels, so models train on a biased, approved-only distribution. We extend LLM-guided reward design, the framework of Qu et al. (2025) in which an LLM evolves the reward of a two-step REINFORCE fraud-blocking policy, to attack this reject-inference problem inside the reward. A single LLM designs a dual-stream reward: stream 1 applies the standard dollar-weighted precision objective to labeled transactions; stream 2 scores legacy-blocked, unlabeled transactions by contrasting the newest gradient-boosted risk signal against the legacy scores that drove the original block. Rather than prescribe which signals matter, we expose a superset of evidence and let the LLM decide for itself which to use, guided by evaluation feedback alone; because it writes the reward as code, that choice is directly auditable. On a held-out four-month out-of-time test, the dual-stream agent beats the prior labeled-only agent at every target recall, by +4.7, +2.4 and +3.0 points of dollar-weighted precision at 80%, 85% and 90% recall, and the production baseline by +6.8 points on average. The resulting policy is architecturally identical to that of Qu et al. (2025) and adds no inference cost.

[NLP-58] Contextuality and Contradictions: Exploring Real-World Identifications of AI-Generated Writing

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决在生成式AI（Generative AI）内容广泛渗透人类互动各领域的背景下，人们如何在实际语境中识别和判断文本是否由人工智能生成这一复杂问题。其核心挑战在于，随着文本来源的不确定性加剧，传统的“人类作者”预设已被打破，导致人们对文本真实性的判断日益依赖于多重、动态且情境化的证据体系。论文的关键解决方案在于结合语言人类学视角，通过定性编码与词汇演变的计算分析，揭示了实际识别过程中所依赖的多样化证据类型——包括具体的文本特征、内容判断、循环推理以及对作者道德品质的假设，并指出这些识别行为本质上并非基于单一技术指标，而是源于一种“语用不妥”（pragmatic infelicity）：即文本元素与特定语境下预期的适切性之间存在的感知错位。因此，真实世界中的AI识别不仅是对“类AI”特征的被动指认，更是一种用于建构和维护社会语言规范的修辞资源，涉及何为可言说、何为恰当乃至何为“人类”的界定。由此，该研究警示：若将生成式内容检测系统设计为脱离具体语境的通用标准，则可能在大规模应用中固化并强化训练数据所反映的特定语境规范，从而加剧社会认知偏见与话语权力的不平等。

作者: Michelle Morgenstern,Julia Witte Zimmerman,Tabia Tanzin Prama,Kristine Harootunian,June Clark,Bryn Loftness,Calla Beauregard,Juniper Lovato
机构: University of Vermont(佛蒙特大学)
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:As AI-generated content spreads into nearly every domain of human interaction, practices and discourses of AI detection, both formal and informal, have become an everyday part of how people interact with text and with each other. In this paper, we explore the real-world practices and discourses of AI identification that have emerged in response to a shifting discursive landscape where the human provenance of a text can no longer be taken for granted. We pair qualitative coding with computational analysis of lexical change, grounded in linguistic anthropological perspectives on language and communication, to investigate AI identifications among English Wikipedia editors and students. We find that these identifications draw on a diversity of evidentiary types, from discrete textual features and judgments about content to circular sense-making claims and presumptions about the author’s moral character, and that they are contradictory, dynamic, and contextually dependent. In practice, what often motivates an AI identification is not the presence of any specific textual element, but pragmatic infelicity: a perceived mismatch between the elements present and those deemed appropriate within the text’s particular context. Consequently, real-world identifications of AI-generated writing do not merely neutrally point out the perceived presence of “AI-like” features, but can be leveraged as a discursive resource to maintain and define sociolinguistic norms: what can be said in a given context, what is appropriate, and, ultimately, what is human. Further, the design and implementation of systems and tools that treat AI-likeness as a context-free property of text may therefore inherit, and enforce at scale, the norms of whichever contexts they were trained on.

[NLP-59] Compression of Emotion in Language Model Representations

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决大语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）在处理细粒度情感分类任务时，其内部表示空间中情感结构组织方式不明确的问题。尽管现有研究已验证LLMs在识别文本情感及生成流畅情感语言方面的能力，但模型输出结果无法揭示其内部对27种细粒度情感类别及其与中性情绪共同构成的28类情感标签的表征机制。论文以GoEmotions数据集为基准，系统评估了七种LLMs在细粒度情感分类、情感家族（emotion-family）和情感极性（sentiment）等不同层级上的表现。研究发现，在未使用情感标签的无监督聚类（基于KMeans协议）条件下，模型隐藏层表示呈现出显著的“过压缩”（overcompression）现象：最清晰的聚类结构仅能区分正负情感两大类，且恢复更粗粒度的情感分组所需的聚类数远少于完整的28类体系。然而，线性探测（linear probes）仍能有效提取大量细粒度情感信息，表明细粒度情感特征虽被压缩，但并未完全丢失。因此，该研究的核心结论是：尽管模型的无监督几何结构主要由宽泛的情绪极性主导，但细粒度情感信息仍保留在内部表示中，其关键在于通过有监督的探测方法可有效挖掘这些潜在表征。

机构: Stanford University (斯坦福大学); Tel Aviv University (特拉维夫大学)
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) have been evaluated on their ability to identify emotions expressed in text and produce fluent emotional language. However, output predictions alone do not reveal how fine-grained emotion distinctions are organized internally. We study seven LLMs on GoEmotions, an English Reddit dataset annotated with 27 fine-grained emotion categories plus neutral. We compare model predictions and emotion-prompted final-token representations with the 28 GoEmotions categories and with coarser emotion-family and sentiment groupings. We find a consistent pattern of \textitovercompression relative to the fine-grained GoEmotions taxonomy. Under the tested KMeans protocol, when we cluster their hidden representations without using emotion labels, the clearest split is into two groups that largely separate positive from negative emotion. Coarser emotion groupings are also recovered with fewer clusters than the full 28-category taxonomy. Yet linear probes retain substantial fine-grained predictive information. These results suggest that fine-grained emotion information remains accessible even though broader affective structure more strongly organizes the unsupervised geometry. [NLP-60] Greedy Byte-Pair Encoding Achieves at Least 0.361 of the Optimal Compression

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决字节对编码（Byte-Pair Encoding, BPE）在文本压缩中通过贪心策略进行符号对合并时，其性能与最优解之间差距的理论边界问题。具体而言，研究关注的是：在给定字符串、合并预算及任意破局规则下，贪心算法所实现的字符串长度缩减量与最优缩减量之比的下界。此前已知该比值至少为1/3，但这一界限长期未被突破。本文首次证明了该比值始终不低于0.361，显著优于之前的1/3下界。关键突破在于揭示了旧有分析框架——即“配对打包松弛”（pair-packing relaxation）——的紧致性（tightness），这解释了为何1/3成为难以逾越的障碍；因此，要获得更优下界必须深入利用最优解的结构特性。作者进一步指出，在贪心策略一次性破坏三个最优合并点的情况下，其中至少一个通常可通过“就近迁移”（moving next door）来补偿，因为最优解中同一规则的所有出现形式具有不可区分性；其余情形则由后续步骤予以弥补。研究过程中，作者精确求解了两次合并的最坏情况比率，给出了三次合并的上界，并最终提炼出一个待验证的单一不等式，该不等式若得证，即可完全解决此问题。

作者: Kundan Baliga,Aiden Xie,Aditya Byju
机构: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (伊利诺伊大学厄本那-香槟分校); Georgia Institute of Technology (佐治亚理工学院)
类目: Data Structures and Algorithms (cs.DS); Computation and Language (cs.CL)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) builds a tokeniser by repeatedly merging a most frequent adjacent pair of symbols; its utility is the total reduction in string length achieved by k merges. It was known that this greedy rule achieves at least a third of the optimal reduction. We prove that it always achieves at least 0.361 of the optimal reduction in string length, for every string, every budget and every tie-breaking rule; this is the first improvement of the bound one third. We also explain why one third was a barrier: the pair-packing relaxation behind it is tight, so a better bound must use more of the optimum’s structure. When greedy destroys three of the optimum’s merge points at once, one of them can usually be moved next door, because all copies of a rule of the optimum look alike; the remaining cases are paid for later. Along the way we determine the worst-case ratio for two merges exactly, bound it for three, and isolate a single inequality that would settle the problem.

[NLP-61] ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决生成式 AI（Generative AI）在大语言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）推理加速过程中，现有推测解码（speculative decoding）方案存在的核心瓶颈问题：传统自回归式推测器（autoregressive drafter）因逐个生成令牌导致推测成本随推测长度线性增长，而扩散式推测器（diffusion drafter）虽可并行生成但忽略了令牌间的依赖关系，从而限制了生成质量与推理效率的平衡。其解决方案的关键在于提出ChainFlow——一种全新的推测解码范式及首个基于目标模型隐藏状态进行流匹配（flow-matching）的推测器。ChainFlow将推测过程建模为对目标隐藏状态空间的短时传输，仅需一到两个流步骤即可完成，远少于传统从噪声中去噪所需的多步迭代；通过变分自编码器（VAE）压缩隐藏状态以实现低开销的推测计算，轻量级反馈头恢复令牌间的上下文依赖关系，并结合树形推测（tree drafting）机制提升接受率。实验表明，在相同推测器规模和训练数据条件下，ChainFlow在vLLM框架下相较于EAGLE-3和DFlash分别实现39%和11%的性能提升，且随着推测器逐步适配新语言，优势进一步扩大。

Abstract:Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. We introduce ChainFlow, a new speculative decoding paradigm and the first flow-matching drafter conditioned on the target’s hidden states. ChainFlow treats drafting as a short transport over hidden states, needing one or two flow steps instead of the many denoising steps of generation from noise. A variational autoencoder compresses these states so drafting cost barely grows with target size, lightweight feedback heads restore inter-token dependencies, and tree drafting raises acceptance. On Qwen3.5 models, at matched drafter size and training data, ChainFlow outperforms EAGLE-3 and DFlash in vLLM by 39% and 11%, respectively. These gains further widen as drafters are adapted to new languages sequentially. Our ablations cover drafter design and concurrent serving, and we open-source our code and drafter models.

[NLP-62] urkish Multimodal Video Fact-Checking: A New Dataset and a Comparison of Zero-Shot Agent ic and Fine-Tuned Systems

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决社交媒体中基于视频的虚假信息在低资源语言（如土耳其语）中缺乏有效事实核查工具的问题。现有事实核查系统几乎全部聚焦于英文文本，导致土耳其语等语言的多模态视频虚假信息难以被准确识别与验证。为此，本文提出了TeViD（土耳其语视频事实核查数据集），据作者所知，这是首个面向土耳其语的多模态视频事实核查数据集。其关键解决方案在于：首先构建了一个高质量、经过平衡的数据集，通过整合国际事实核查网络（IFCN）认证机构发布的文章，并融合翻译自Snopes的案例及合成样本以缓解类别不平衡；其次，提出两种基于同一开源基础模型的验证管道——3MFact-TR（Pipeline 1）与微调模型（Pipeline 2）。其中，3MFact-TR采用Qwen2.5-7B大语言模型与Qwen2-VL-7B视觉-语言模型，引入语义不一致检测器、5W1H问题管理模块及双语证据检索器（排除已知事实核查网站以防止泄露）；而微调模型则利用低秩适应（LoRA）对单一Qwen2.5-7B模型进行微调，实现仅依赖声明与视频文本描述的闭卷判断。实验结果表明，该方案在准确性、宏平均F1、真类F1及真类召回率等方面均表现出色，并通过消融实验验证了各组件的有效性。

Abstract:Video-based misinformation spreads rapidly on social media, but almost all existing fact-checking systems focus exclusively on English text. Tools for low-resource languages such as Turkish are severely limited. In this work, we present TeViD (Turkish Video Fact-checking Dataset), to the best of our knowledge the first multimodal video fact-checking dataset for Turkish. We compiled the dataset from articles published by this http URL, an IFCN-certified organisation, and enriched it with translated Snopes articles and synthetic examples to reduce class imbalance. Building on TeViD, we develop two verification pipelines that share the same open-source base model. First, in 3MFact-TR (Pipeline 1), we adapt the multi-role 3MFact framework to Turkish with the Qwen2.5-7B large language model and the Qwen2-VL-7B vision-language model, and add three modules of our own: a semantic inconsistency checker, a 5W1H question manager, and a bilingual evidence retriever that excludes fact-checking sites to prevent leakage. Second, as our Fine-Tuned Model (Pipeline 2), we fine-tune a single Qwen2.5-7B with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to produce closed-book verdicts from the claim and the video’s textual description. We report accuracy, macro F1, True class F1, and True class recall for both systems, together with ablation studies.

[NLP-63] FinEvolveKG: Controlled and Attributable Prompt Evolution for Financial Knowledge Graph Construction

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决金融领域知识图谱（Knowledge Graph, KG）构建中，如何在保持共享基础结构（如实体类型、时间规则等）一致性的同时，灵活适应不同用户角色（persona）的分析需求这一关键挑战。现有方法依赖人工编写提示词或微调模型，成本高昂且易导致共享规则被意外修改；而无约束的全量提示优化虽具灵活性，却可能混淆通用规则与角色特定策略的演化路径，降低可解释性与可审查性。为此，论文提出FinEvolveKG框架，其核心创新在于将提示词结构解耦为可复用的通用块（general block）与可独立版本化的角色策略块（persona policy block），并通过机械约束机制确保生成式进化提示优化器（GEPA）仅作用于角色策略块，从而实现“可追溯的演化”——通用块保持字节级稳定，所有优化操作均局部化、可追踪。该方案采用双目标优化：兼顾通用时序知识图谱质量与角色相关事实、主题及多跳连通性。实验在不重叠股票代码的10-K文本分割上验证五种变异范围，三组角色条件分支（v3-v5）分别进行三次种子测试。结果表明，完整两阶段受限工作流（v4）相较冻结提示基线（v1）提升19.4%-30.9%，优于无约束全提示流程（v5）2.2%-6.4%，并在两个目标组件上均领先，九组配对种子比较中全部胜出，且种子方差最低。此外，未进一步优化下，v4在所有分布外（OOD）迁移场景中亦优于v5。专家审计支持生成三元组作为真实标签，双专家盲审中v4在70.1%的对比增强判断中胜出。研究表明，通过机械化的边界约束实现提示演化的可归因性，可在不牺牲性能的前提下达成强实证效果，且性能提升并非由边界本身直接导致。

Abstract:Financial institutions construct knowledge graphs (KGs) from shared SEC 10-Ks to serve risk analysis, portfolio management, and investment research, whose analytical needs differ. Extraction must adapt without fragmenting shared grounding, typing, and temporal rules. Hand-authored persona prompts and fine-tuning add cost. Weight-free prompt optimization offers an alternative, but unconstrained evolution of a monolithic prompt can rewrite shared rules alongside persona guidance, obscuring changes and complicating review. We introduce FinEvolveKG, a KG-construction harness separating reusable general and persona-policy blocks and mechanically confining GEPA, a reflective prompt optimizer, to the designated block. During persona adaptation, the approved general block remains byte-stable and every optimizer edit is localized to a separately versioned persona policy. A dual objective balances generic temporal-KG quality with persona-relevant facts, motifs, and multi-hop connectivity. We evaluate five mutation scopes on ticker-disjoint 10-K splits, with three seeds for the persona-conditioned arms (v3-v5) across three personas. On the three-seed mean, the complete two-stage block-constrained workflow (v4) improves over the frozen prompt baseline (v1) by 19.4-30.9% and over the tested unconstrained full-prompt workflow (v5) by 2.2-6.4%, leading v5 on both objective components and winning all nine paired-seed comparisons with the lowest seed variance in every persona. Without further optimization, v4 also exceeds v5 across all evaluated out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts. An SME audit supports using the generated triplets as ground truth; a blinded two-SME audit favors v4 over v5 in 70.1% of contrast-enriched judgments. These results show that mechanically attributable evolution can coexist with strong empirical performance, without attributing the gains causally to the boundary.

[NLP-64] Forcing a Letter Suppresses Refusal: Mechanistic Evidence from WMDP EMNLP2026

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决大语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）安全评估中普遍采用的多选题（Multiple-Choice Question, MCQ）格式可能导致模型拒绝不当请求行为被低估的问题。研究表明，MCQ格式会显著降低模型的拒绝率，从而可能误导对模型安全机制的真实评估。其解决方案的关键在于揭示了MCQ格式影响安全行为的内在机制：首先，通过调谐透镜（tuned lens）技术发现，模型在处理MCQ时会迅速锁定答案选项对应的词元，而开放问答格式下拒绝意图则呈现渐进式积累；其次，观测到MCQ格式下的激活向量与拒绝方向之间的距离约为开放格式的3倍，表明模型在MCQ中更远离拒绝状态；最后，消融分析显示，移除承载MCQ答案选择的注意力头会提高拒绝率，直接证明答案选择过程与拒绝机制存在竞争关系。这些发现共同表明，当前基于MCQ的安全评估主要反映的是模型的知识能力而非真实的安全防御机制。

Abstract:Safety benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) commonly use multiple-choice question (MCQ) format. However, prior studies documented that MCQ format reduces refusal rates, which may significantly affect the safety behavior of the model. We provide a first mechanistic explanation of this effect on the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP) dataset across two models - Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. First, we use the tuned lens technique to show that when processing MCQ the model commits to an answer-letter token very quickly, which is in contrast to the gradual refusal build-up in open-ended formats. Additionally, we observe that activations on the MCQ format lie roughly 3x further from the refusal direction, compared with their open-ended counterparts. Moreover, ablating the attention heads that carry the MCQ format answer increases the refusal, which is a direct evidence that the MCQ answer-selection competes with refusal. These findings indicate that MCQ safety scores primarily measure knowledge capabilities and do not assess the safety-mechanisms.

[NLP-65] How Small Can We Go? Calibrating Activation-Cache Compression for SAE Training NEURIPS2026

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决在训练稀疏自编码器（Sparse Autoencoder, SAE）过程中，模型激活值缓存压缩对特征保留能力的影响问题。核心挑战在于：如何在降低存储开销的同时，尽可能保持原始高精度激活中所蕴含的语义特征结构。其解决方案的关键在于提出一种基于“校准”的量化评估框架——通过设定“重训练相同字节集”作为性能上限（天花板）和“随机种子重置”作为下限（地板），从而为不同压缩方法提供与其所在场景相匹配的基准对比标准。在此基础上，研究发现：简单地采用每令牌4比特整数量化（int4）会显著损失特征，远低于随机种子重置带来的基线；而通过在量化前对通道进行标准化处理，可使int4在保留特征方面超越自身场景下的最低基准，且维持相同的文件大小。此外，实验表明，使用bf16前向传播虽节省内存，但特征保留能力略逊于旋转8比特存储。整体方案强调了评估压缩影响时需考虑上下文依赖性，并引入校准机制以实现更公平、可靠的比较。

Abstract:To train a sparse autoencoder (SAE), you need a massive cache of model activations. We look into the effects that compression has on an SAE in two ways: we keep the original fp32-trained SAE and pass the compressed cache into the same SAE to see how many feature activations stay the same (the frozen-SAE test), and we retrain an SAE on the compressed cache and see how many of the original features still exist (the retraining test). We found that in the retraining test, there is no clear scale for retained features. On a GPT-2 cache, rounding everything to fp16 keeps 60.6% of features, but changing one value in a million by the smallest step fp32 allows (a change eight orders of magnitude smaller) keeps only 70.5%. Meanwhile, changing the random seed keeps 23.0%. For the frozen-SAE test, the frozen SAE’s correlation with the original increases in order of how precise the codecs are, but plain L_2 distance gives nearly the same ordering. We also see the same frozen reading correspond to different percentages retained at different sites. This leaves the question of the right measurement. We build one by calibrating: retraining on identical bytes sets the ceiling, and a reseed sets the floor. We then measure the effect of each compressed codec against its own site’s floor. With TopK SAEs on GPT-2 small and Pythia-1.4B at research-scale budgets, naïve per-token int4 loses more features than a reseed everywhere we tested, as do PCA and random projection on GPT-2. Standardizing each channel before quantizing brings int4 back above the floor in terms of retained features, at the same raw file size. At our smallest budget, a bf16 forward pass, which some pipelines use to save memory, loses slightly more features than rotated 8-bit storage. Calibrating a site costs four training runs and two evaluation passes.

[NLP-66] Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models WACV2027

【速读】： 该论文旨在探究生成式视觉-语言模型（Vision-Language Models, VLMs）中是否存在类似大语言模型中的隐性学习（subliminal learning）现象，即教师模型通过与目标偏好无关的训练数据，将隐藏偏好传递给学生模型。其核心问题是：在不直接涉及特定偏好任务的情况下，VLM是否仍会无意识地吸收并复制教师模型的隐含偏好？解决方案的关键在于设计一个控制实验范式——使用同一基础模型微调出具有特定动物或面部属性偏好的“有偏教师”模型，以及一个无偏的“控制教师”模型；二者均生成与目标任务（几何形状识别）无关的数值输出，随后两个从相同基础模型初始化的学生模型分别基于这些数值进行微调。研究发现，无论是在动物偏好还是面部属性偏好任务中，学生模型均能有效继承教师的隐性偏好，且性能差异可达约10个百分点。此外，有偏学生模型在解释其决策时，使用的词汇和短语模式更接近有偏教师，即使三者选择相同的图像。这表明，训练数据的间接影响可导致模型偏好及解释行为的系统性偏差，且这种转移效应随训练数据量增加而增强。该研究揭示了在跨模态训练中潜在的隐性偏见传播风险，对VLM的训练策略与公平性评估具有重要意义。

机构: Johns Hopkins University (约翰霍普金斯大学); Baltimore, MD, USA

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. We study whether subliminal learning also occurs in vision-language models (VLMs). We finetune a teacher VLM to prefer a specific animal or facial attribute and use a control teacher from the same base model. Both teachers generate numbers for an unrelated visual task involving geometric shapes. Two students initialized from the same base VLM are finetuned on the same images, using numbers generated by either the biased or control teacher. Across VLMs ranging from 2B to 7B parameters, we find that both animal and facial preferences can transfer through this unrelated task. Students trained on biased-teacher outputs select the target more often than control students, with a difference of up to \sim 10 percentage points in the animal preference task. Transfer can become stronger with more training data and varies with the target preference, model, and how the numbers are generated. Beyond preferences, we show that the biased student’s explanations use more of the same words and phrases as the biased teacher’s explanations than those of the control student, even when all three models select the same image. These results matter for training VLMs and show that training on unrelated data may change both a VLM’s image preferences and how it explains its choices, and that transfer can become stronger with more training samples.

[NLP-67] Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决大语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）及多模态大语言模型（Large Vision-Language Models, LVLMs）在指令微调过程中因依赖海量训练数据所导致的高计算与存储成本问题，同时应对训练数据中存在的冗余、噪声及低质量样本等挑战。现有数据选择方法通常基于多样性或重要性，但未能显式约束所选子集与全量数据在嵌入空间中的分布一致性。为此，本文提出一种质量感知的多频带特征函数匹配方法（QMAC），其核心在于将数据选择建模为分布匹配与质量过滤的联合优化问题：通过在多个频率尺度上匹配所选子集与全量数据的经验特征函数，有效捕捉全局语义覆盖与局部扰动特性；同时结合任务相关的质量评分机制，过滤噪声和低质量样本。实验在四种数据类型、八种目标模型及四十四项基准上系统评估，结果表明，QMAC在标准图文指令数据上优于现有基线，在文本指令、图文推理及文本推理数据上显著超越随机采样，并在多种模型与预算组合下实现对全量数据训练的性能超越，验证了其高效性与优越性。

类目: Machine Learning (cs.LG); Computation and Language (cs.CL)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Instruction tuning of large language models and large vision language models relies on massive training data, which incurs substantial computational and storage costs. Meanwhile, training data often contains redundancy, noise, and low quality samples. Existing data selection methods mostly rely on diversity, importance, or a combination of both, without explicitly constraining the distributional consistency between the selected subset and the full data in the embedding space. We propose QMAC, a quality aware multiband characteristic function matching method that formulates data selection as a joint optimization problem of distribution matching and quality filtering. QMAC matches the empirical characteristic functions of the selected subset and the full data across multiple frequency scales, capturing both global semantic coverage and local perturbations, while using task related quality scores to filter noisy and low quality samples. We systematically evaluate QMAC on 4 data types, 8 target models, and 44 benchmarks. Experimental results show that QMAC outperforms existing data selection baselines on standard image-text instruction data, substantially surpasses random selection on standard text instruction, image-text reasoning, and text reasoning data, and exceeds full data training in multiple model and budget combinations. The code will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the paper.

[NLP-68] Same Question Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLM s on Smoking-Cessation Advice

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决生成式 AI（Generative AI）在健康咨询场景中存在个性化偏差的问题，即不同用户角色（如年龄、专业背景、吸烟史等）所获得的医疗建议是否存在系统性差异。研究通过向六家主流厂商部署的大型语言模型（LLM）提出相同的戒烟咨询问题，针对12种具有不同生命阶段、自我描述专业程度和吸烟史的用户人格化角色（persona），共生成2,880条响应进行审计。结果显示，模型对青少年用户提及美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准的处方戒烟药物的比例显著低于对成年用户的提及率，降幅达32至67个百分点；且在五款模型中，呈现医疗专业背景的角色反而获得的信息量少于无专业知识的角色。这一发现揭示了当前生成式AI在临床建议输出中存在显著的人格化偏倚。其解决方案的关键在于引入一个可部署的干预措施——在系统提示中加入“事实底线”（factual floor），即要求所有用户在相关情境下均应接收到一组核心医学事实，同时允许语气、词汇和表达方式自由调整以适应不同用户。实验表明，该提示能有效缩小不同人格化角色间的差异，但其提升整体事实覆盖率的效果在不同模型间表现不一，且方向各异，说明该干预措施不具备跨模型通用性。研究进一步指出两个重要警示：一是“等量提及”并非理想临床目标，因未成年人不宜使用某些处方药物，因此事实底线必须具备年龄敏感性；二是由于人格化角色在多个维度上同时变化，研究仅报告情景层面的整体差异，而非孤立分析单一因素的影响。研究已公开全部2,880条响应数据与分析代码，为后续可解释性与公平性评估提供基础。

Abstract:Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice? We audit six widely deployed LLMs from four providers on smoking cessation, a domain with codified clini- cal guidance and substantial public-health stakes, by putting the same four cessation questions to twelve user personas that differ in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, for a total of 2,880 responses. What the models say depends on who appears to be asking. Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none. We then evaluate one deployable intervention: a short system prompt specifying a factual floor, the set of core med- ical facts every user should receive when they are relevant, while leaving tone, vocabulary, and framing free to adapt. The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another. Two cautions frame these results. Equal mention rates are not always the correct clinical target, because prescription cessation pharmacother- apy is not recommended for minors, so a defensible factual floor must be age-aware rather than uniform. And because our personas vary on several attributes at once, we report scenario- level differences rather than isolated effects of age or expertise. We release all 2,880 responses and the analysis code.

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) have made fluent essay writing, code drafting, and quiz answering instantly available to students at every level, from secondary school through graduate study. Many educators do not object to LLM use \emphper~se; what they need to detect is the case in which a student pastes the assignment prompt into a chatbot and submits the model’s reply verbatim, without engaging with the work. Existing post-hoc AI-text detectors remain unreliable and have been shown to penalise non-native English writers, while output-side watermarks require cooperation from the model provider. We propose an alternative that the educator controls directly: an input-side watermark in which an invisible instruction is embedded inside the visible assignment prompt itself. An LLM that ingests the prompt verbatim quietly reads the hidden instruction and writes a tell-tale signature into its reply, exposing the copy-and-paste pathway specifically. We describe SteganoPrompt, a single-page, zero-dependency web tool that encodes an arbitrary printable-ASCII payload into the deprecated Unicode Tags block (\textttU+E0000–\textttU+E007F). The encoded string is visually identical to the original, survives common copy-paste channels (Word, Google Docs, PDF, Markdown, Slack, e-mail, the major learning-management systems), and is tokenized as ordinary text by most frontier models. We evaluate compliance across eight LLM families and a representative set of educational content channels. To keep deployment transparent, disclosure is built into the tool itself: every encoded brief also carries a brief, always-on academic-integrity reminder for the student, and we set out concrete guidance recommending for its disclosed, ethical use in the classroom. The tool is released under the MIT licence at this https URL.

Abstract:This paper presents a novel approach to e-commerce payment fraud detection by integrating reinforcement learning (RL) with Large Language Models (LLMs). By framing transaction risk as a multi-step Markov Decision Process (MDP), RL optimizes risk detection across multiple payment stages. Crafting effective reward functions, essential for RL model success, typically requires significant human expertise due to the complexity and variability in design. LLMs, with their advanced reasoning and coding capabilities, are well-suited to refine these functions, offering improvements over traditional methods. Our approach leverages LLMs to iteratively enhance reward functions, achieving better fraud detection accuracy and demonstrating zero-shot capability. Experiments with real-world data confirm the effectiveness, robustness, and resilience of our LLM-enhanced RL framework through long-term evaluations, underscoring the potential of LLMs in advancing industrial RL applications.

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决神经种群测量维度中“代码成分”与“测量过程本身所引入的噪声或伪影”之间的区分问题，即在观测到的高维数据中，有多少维度真正反映了神经编码的内在结构，又有多少是由于采样方法或测量手段造成的系统性偏差。其核心挑战在于传统维度度量（如参与比）对测量方式高度敏感，难以区分真实信息结构与采样噪声。解决方案的关键在于提出一种轴向解析的维度尺度分析方法（axis-resolved measurement），通过将测得的维度斜率分解为两个部分：一是由采样过程决定的“采样底噪”（sampling floor），二是沿特定物理或语义轴（如刺激方向、神经元数量、语法结构等）获得的“可解释偏移量”（shift）。该方法利用双重零假设检验——标签随机置换和仅在同质样本内置换——来验证偏移量是否具有统计显著性，并揭示其背后的结构。在小鼠视觉皮层V1中，该方法识别出方向选择性神经元驱动的奇数阶分量维持了编码梯度的持续上升能力，而偶数阶分量则决定了编码起始顺序及对称性；在语言模型中，该方法分离出由输入词元继承的内容与由网络深度构建的句法结构，证实了高达20个标准差的语法信号完全源于特征组合而非独立表征。因此，该研究提供了一个无需训练探针、可逐层应用于任意神经数组或Hugging Face模型的通用工具（rung），实现对系统内部代码结构的精确解耦。

Abstract:How much of a neural population’s measured dimensionality is the code, and how much is the act of measuring it? The slope of the participation ratio against subsample size is reported for cortical populations and for the layers of language models as a number that belongs to the system. It does not. One patch of eleven thousand mouse V1 neurons returns three slopes, 0.25 along random stimulus subsets, 0.31 along drift direction, 0.35 along neuron count, and only the middle one carries structure; the other two are the sampling floor. We split every exponent into that floor and a shift earned along a declared axis, and read the shift against two nulls: permuting the labels, and permuting them only among samples that share a nuisance. On V1 the direction-aligned shift clears the label null in eight of eight grating recordings, is positive in 32 of 32 animals in a second laboratory, and reads both sectors of the code’s O(2) symmetry. The even sector sets how the ladder starts: it decides which order of adding classes climbs faster, predicts the opposite order in an equivariant network, and flows under coarse-graining by a closed-form factor that says what orientation columns do to mesoscale signals. The odd sector, carried by the direction-selective neurons, keeps the ladder climbing past half the classes. On language models the same split separates content inherited from the tokens from construction built with depth, on five architectures, and the second null shows that a grammaticality signal of twenty standard deviations is entirely carrier composition. With a floor and a declared axis, dimensionality scaling is an axis-resolved measurement, and where the axis follows a known symmetry it resolves the sector content of the code. The instrument, rung, trains no probe and reads any array or any Hugging Face model layer by layer (this https URL). Comments: 63 pages, 20 figures. 链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09728
作者: Weiqing Zeng,Zida Yang,Guquan You,Jiexin Zheng,Cong Wang
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR)
备注: 14 pages, 2 figures, including 3 pages of supplementary material

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Recommendation systems often enter a new serving window before enough outcomes are available to retrain the deployed model. We study this regime with 0.05-1.0% target feedback, a range that spans our stress tests while keeping supervision far below the degrees of freedom of the source recommender. At this scale, existing fine-tuning and meta-learning methods still estimate target-specific updates from extremely sparse feedback, leaving the update direction weakly identified. SAGE-PAIR instead transfers a source-supported residual correction space and only calibrates this space using target outcomes. We introduce SAGE-PAIR, a staged adapter that pretrains a low-dimensional global residual on an adjacent source period and adds a soft router over residual experts conditioned on source user profiles. Target feedback then calibrates this residual state rather than relearning the recommender. On a locked test split of KuaiSAR-v2, SAGE-PAIR (Full) achieves a 1.77% relative improvement in NDCG@10, while a core-protocol comparison shows a further 0.25% gain from routed experts beyond source-pretrained PAIR. Matched source-pretrained LoRA and Adapter-Tuning baselines remain near the source model, supporting the need for a different adaptation space. Thus, SAGE-PAIR improves ranking quality with millisecond-scale adaptation and inference costs. Sparse-feedback adaptation is fundamentally governed by the identifiability of the update space rather than by label count alone. Source pretraining supplies estimable correction directions for scarce labels, while user-conditioned routing contributes a consistent, differentiated cross-user correction on top of the global correction. Our code is available at this https URL.

[IR-1] SPARSEUP: Towards Better Recipes for Training Modern Learned Sparse Retrievers

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09680
作者: Thibault Formal,Pierre Erbacher,Cosimo Rulli
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Learned sparse embeddings are a powerful alternative to dense retrieval, yet they have fallen behind single-vector and late interaction models. One reason for their limited adoption is that they are notoriously difficult to train, generally requiring very tight conditions to converge. We present a recipe for training Splade-like encoders on modern backbones and data that achieves a better efficiency-effectiveness trade-off. We discuss the role of logit distribution and its impact on the training stability and the final sparsity of the encoder. We also introduce a new per-position fan-out control - a hard cap on how many vocabulary dimensions each position may emit. We further apply a simple vocabulary merging strategy that removes redundant entries - such as case and word-boundary variants of the same word - which are common in cased BPE-based backbones. We apply our recipe to the LateOn backbone and training data, obtaining SPARSEUP, a sparse encoder that reaches 56.4 average nDCG@10 on BEIR-13, the highest we know of among public vocabulary-based sparse encoders below 150M parameters.

[IR-2] ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09472
作者: Ruiyi Yang,Zechen Li,Lihuan Li,Du Yin,Hao Xue,Flora D. Salim
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Information Retrieval (cs.IR)
备注: 22 pages, 4 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Language-model agents use experience through external retrieval and parameter learning. Consolidating stored experience into model weights requires deciding both which experience to train on and when its external records can leave retrieval. Admission based solely on student mastery can exclude useful teacher demonstrations, while removal immediately after training can discard guidance that the model still needs. We introduce ENGRAM, a framework that separates training admission from memory release. A demonstration-aware gate admits skills based on student mastery or sufficient successful teacher demonstrations. The student learns from selected action traces with context from an Engram Trace Graph (ETG). A verification gate then compares the updated model without episodic retrieval against the base model with retrieval on reserved probes. Release requires valid training participation and scores meeting both relative and absolute criteria; records for skills that fail verification remain retrievable. Experiments across interactive and reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over frozen-weight ETG controls, with ablations supporting demonstration-aware admission and selective adapter activation. A controlled held-out comparison shows that verified release substantially reduces the retrievable footprint while remaining close to retain-all performance and outperforming immediate and budget-matched random release. ENGRAM also improves task performance while reducing input-token usage and model calls. Skill-level verification further reduces retrievable experience through selective archival, retaining external guidance for skills that do not meet the release criteria. Code is available in this http URL.

[IR-3] Orthogonal Norm Growth in Two-Tower Retrieval: A Popularity Mechanism for Unified Discovery RECSYS2026

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09294
作者: Andrei Atamaniuk
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR)
备注: 6 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at USRW 2026 (non-archival), co-located with ACM RecSys 2026. Supplementary material included as an ancillary file. Workshop: this https URL . Code: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Unified search and recommendation systems may update the same item vectors from both interaction streams. We study how repeated updates can increase an item vector’s norm and affect retrieval under an unnormalized dot product. A cosine-only loss makes the output gradient perpendicular to the current item vector - tangent to its constant-norm sphere. Training changes encoder parameters, however, so the realized item-vector movement need not remain tangent. We derive sufficient conditions under which it does; every nonzero update then increases squared norm by its squared length. When the tasks share an item encoder, sequential updates from both can accumulate in the same norm, which raw-inner-product serving can expose for either task. This conditional result is not a theorem about joint SGD. Controlled ablations test these conditions. On MovieLens 32M and Amazon Books, accumulated tangent movement accompanies frequency-norm association and additional head-item exposure under raw-dot rather than normalized-item ranking. In a nonlinear tower combining a per-item ID vector with a shared content encoding, active item movement remains near-tangent. We separate its norm change into the ID-update contribution and other output changes, then use a matched training intervention that removes immediate norm growth caused by the ID-row update. The intervention reduces norm-related exposure but also recommendation utility, so it is diagnostic rather than a proposed mitigation. Our logs are recommendation-only: the formulation supplies a shared-representation audit, while prevalence in joint traffic remains open.

[IR-4] FondueQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating Parametric Compensation in Multi-Hop QA

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09274
作者: Laurin Schmid,Suman Navaratnarajah,Koel Dutta Chowdhury,Steffen Eger,Josif Grabocka,Christian Frey
类目: Machine Learning (cs.LG); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Information Retrieval (cs.IR)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Large Language Models (LLMs) show remarkable performance based on parametric knowledge, i.e., their ability to recall facts and associations internalized in a model’s weights. However, studying this capability on established multi-hop benchmarks may be complicated by benchmark contamination, as many of these benchmarks have been publicly available long enough to plausibly appear in modern pretraining corpora. As a result, correct answers under missing evidence may reflect either general parametric knowledge or memorization of benchmark-specific instances. To study how models use internal knowledge when retrieval evidence is incomplete, we introduce FondueQA, in which every required multi-hop fact is uniquely localized to a designated evidence document. This enables controlled document-level evidence ablations to study parametric compensation under incomplete retrieval. Our empirical evaluation reveals that parametric compensation strongly depends on both entity popularity and the structural role of missing evidence. Generally, models compensate more successfully for facts involving popular entities. On FondueQA, we show that bridging evidence can be more useful than the answer-bearing document itself. Moreover, models may recall a missing fact in isolation but fail to use it under partial evidence, particularly when the context contains plausible competing entities, which can reduce Exact Match by up to 15 percentage points.

Abstract:Patent analytics increasingly relies on transformer representations and large language models (LLMs), yet linking conceptual classification, topic formation and interpretation requires explicit decisions about model roles and the evidence retained at each stage. In this design-oriented study, we propose and demonstrate a patent analytics pipeline that links these tasks and keeps each decision open to audit. Three LLMs separately classify each patent by novelty (radical or incremental) and innovation type (product, process, service). Radical and innovation-type labels each require two supporting votes, with Incremental used as the fallback novelty label. Topics are discovered by clustering PatentSBERTa embeddings, with parameter ranges scaled to corpus size. A patent-specific stopword list is applied only when topics are represented with class-based term frequency–inverse document frequency (c-TF-IDF), and a second embedding model supports inter-topic similarity, hierarchical refinement and visualization. An LLM then labels each topic from its ranked keywords and representative patents. We demonstrate the pipeline on 30,964 public-sector-related patents retrieved from this http URL. Across five category corpora ranging from 591 to 29,215 patents, the pipeline produced 74 category-specific topic instances with a macro-average document coverage of 98.1% and topic diversity of 0.900–1.000, and fewer than 1% of classification outputs returned UNKNOWN. Because every model vote and the evidence behind each topic label are retained, analysts can audit and revise the outputs. The demonstration establishes the feasibility and traceability of the pipeline; testing its labels against expert coding and benchmarking it against alternative pipelines are identified as the next steps. The pipeline offers a reusable basis for LLM-assisted patent analysis in technology intelligence.

Abstract:While machine learning hiring tools are ubiquitous, the need for privacy regulations and commercial sensitivity makes public benchmarking legally complex. Abstract:Explainable scholar recommendation aims to identify potential scholars of interest and provide reasonable explanations for the recommendations. However, existing frameworks struggle with optimization-induced noise and “hub node bias”, yielding trivial explanations that lack hierarchical depth and personalization. To this end, we propose a novel explainable scholar recommendation model, Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning (named PAGSL). PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31% in F1-score, 6.29% in Accuracy and 5.95% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. PAGSL achieves strong performance in both recommendation accuracy and explainability.

[IR-9] MV-IVF: Multi-Vector Retrieval via Multi-Vector Clustering

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09040
作者: Kishen N Gowda,Laxman Dhulipala,Lars Gottesbüren,Rajesh Jayaram
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR); Databases (cs.DB)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Multi-vector retrieval represents each query and document as a set of embeddings and scores relevance via fine-grained set-to-set interactions such as MaxSim (Chamfer similarity). This expressiveness improves retrieval quality over single-vector representations, but makes search substantially more expensive. Existing systems address this challenge primarily through proxy representations or filter-and-rerank pipelines that reduce candidate generation to single-vector search. We study the complementary direction of building a native IVF-style index directly over multi-vector data. We introduce MV-IVF, an inverted-file index for multi-vector retrieval built on MV-Lloyd, a new Lloyd-style algorithm for clustering point clouds under a Chamfer objective. Our key observation is that once point clouds are assigned to clusters, the center-update step reduces to standard single-vector clustering over the flattened embeddings in each cluster. This enables efficient construction of a hierarchical IVF tree with center point clouds at internal nodes. At query time, MV-IVF performs best-first beam search over the tree to identify promising leaf clusters, then scores the documents in those leaves. We further accelerate search using low-bit quantization, query compression, and cache-efficient batched search. We implement MV-IVF in MVSIC, an optimized C++ library and unified evaluation framework for multi-vector retrieval that includes several major approaches. Across BEIR and LoTTE text retrieval benchmarks, MV-IVF achieves strong latency–recall tradeoffs, the best batched throughput frontiers, and favorable build-time and index-size profiles. At 90% Recall- 10 @ 10 , MV-IVF achieves up to 8.03\times lower single-query latency and up to 173.5\times higher QPS than the baselines, demonstrating that native IVF-style indexing is practical and effective for scalable multi-vector retrieval. Abstract:Latent reasoning in generative recommendation faces two practical barriers: constructing teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision is costly, and recurrent hidden-state feedback requires a specialized execution loop. We revisit both the supervision source and the computation interface. A step-level diagnosis measures how recommendation CoT supports next-item prediction and trace coherence. In the analyzed traces, history analysis is the only step with positive mean contributions on both dimensions, while later preference and intent steps have negative mean answer contributions. PHiT aggregates cached sparse item encodings to construct these targets and supervises the contextual states of distinct vocabulary thought tokens. All thought tokens are supplied together as ordinary input IDs during a single causal prefill, removing the need for recurrent final-state feedback. With supervised fine-tuning alone, PHiT outperforms the compared baselines across four recommendation benchmarks. Controlled ablations support the value of input-matched semantic supervision, while cost measurements show fast target construction with training time comparable to the recommendation-only thought-token baseline.

Abstract:Reliable dermatology AI requires access to verifiable evidence distributed across heterogeneous textual and visual sources. Through eight hierarchical graph-probing tools, the orchestrator progressively identifies relevant entities, inspects node-level information, traverses relations and paths, and retrieves source-text and visual evidence. This progressive-disclosure design allows the model to adaptively determine the retrieval modality, exploration direction, and evidence granularity while constructing a query-specific evidence subgraph. Abstract:Search and recommendation at Shopify require retrieving relevant products from a changing catalog of billions of products under strict latency constraints. We show that reinforcement learning further improves judged search relevance. Furthermore, distillation from task-specific experts improves recommendation quality over joint supervised fine-tuning without a statistically detected loss in search quality. Finally, for efficient serving, we pair multi-token prediction with a lightweight ranker, improving retrieval quality over our autoregressive baseline while reducing latency. We evaluate SID-LLM both as a standalone retriever and as a component of Shopify’s production search and recommendation systems. As a standalone search system, SID-LLM achieves quality comparable to Shopify’s existing multi-model search stack while meeting production latency requirements. Integrating SID-LLM into the search and recommendation stacks provides significant gains in both offline evaluations and online A/B tests. Together, these results demonstrate the practical value of semantic-ID generation as a unified approach to product discovery at scale.

Abstract:Generative recommendation aims to predict item identifiers from user interaction histories, but explicit control over the properties of recommended items remains underexplored. To address this, we propose Steerable Generative Recommender (SteerGR), a framework that uses sparse autoencoders for concept-level control in game discovery. SteerGR proceeds through three stages: (i) Concept Definition and Grounding for defining play concepts with an LLM; (ii) Feature Discovery and Selection for discovering candidate features by their concept associations and selecting one by its steering effect; and (iii) Sparse Feature Intervention for amplifying or suppressing selected features to steer recommendations without retraining the recommender. Extensive experiments with two industrial generative recommendation models on a real-world game dataset show that the selected features successfully steer recommendations toward or away from target concepts. We believe this work takes a first step to extend SAE-based steering from LLMs to industrial generative recommendation.

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) are attractive rerankers for recommendation. Running an expensive model on every request is costly, and for users with sparse interaction histories it often lowers quality. We present CascadeRec, a two-tier LLM reranking cascade deployed in production at a large financial planning and analysis (FPA) SaaS provider. It serves content recommendations to enterprise tenants on AWS EKS and GKE. A lightweight Tier-1 model reranks every request. A router escalates only the requests where extra inference-time compute is likely to help, and sends them to a more expensive Tier-2 procedure (self-consistency sampling, multi-path reasoning, or a larger model). The system has run in a production A/B experiment for over a month. Compared with uniform use of the expensive tier, CascadeRec has reduced inference cost by about 10%, with minimal latency impact and no quality regression observed to date. Tenant data cannot be released, so we also evaluate the pipeline on public benchmarks (MovieLens-1M and Amazon-Electronics). Segment-level analysis with paired-bootstrap confidence intervals shows that uniform LLM reranking lowers NDCG@10 for sparse-history users by up to 30%, and its only statistically significant gain appears on the segment with the longest histories. Escalating cold users can make the loss larger instead of repairing it. Which segments benefit from escalation depends on the domain, and this motivates the segment-gated rollout we use in production. We describe the deployment architecture, the measured benefits, and lessons learned, including inter-tenant load imbalance as a driver for cascading and the handling of LLM output-parsing failures at the serving layer.

[IR-15] RedMall: Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale E-commerce

作者: Kunyang Zhou,Xin Jia,Yi Yang,Yongjun Yang,Manjie Xu,Honglei Zhang,Yan Zhu,Kai Zuo,Xu Tang,Zheng Wang

Abstract:Generative recommendation has shown considerable potential in industrial recommendation systems. However, the performance of existing generative methods is limited by several challenges. 1) Semantic IDs (SIDs) are treated as one-dimensional sequences, overlooking the hierarchical dependencies among different layers. 2) Next-token prediction used is unable to explicitly optimize session-wise recommendation. 3) Although reinforcement learning has been applied to align generated recommendations with user preferences, few existing methods explicitly optimize the ranking of positive items in session-wise recommendation. To address the above issues, we propose RedMall, a generative recommender designed for large-scale e-commerce. Firstly, RedMall constructs hierarchical SIDs through residual quantization over multimodal representations. Secondly, RedMall introduces a lightweight SID encoder to explicitly model layer-wise dependencies in SIDs. Moreover, RedMall incorporates sparse mixture-of-experts, dual gated attention, and multi-target prediction to scale model size, enhance user interest representation, and optimize session-wise recommendation. We further design an exposure-aware loss that treats exposed but unclicked items as negative feedback. To better align user preferences and list-wise ranking objectives, we combine Group Relative Policy Optimization with an auxiliary LambdaRank loss, using both real user feedback and item ranking to guide optimization. Experiments on four public datasets-Amazon Beauty, Amazon Toys, Amazon Food, and MovieLens-1M—show that RedMall outperforms the evaluated baselines across all reported Recall and NDCG metrics. Online A/B tests show improvements of 2.24% in advertiser value (ADVV) and 0.59% in click-through rate (CTR) for e-commerce advertising, as well as gains of 1.08% in GMV and 0.95% in daily active buyers (DAB) for e-commerce recommendations.

Abstract:The vast amount of information available in lengthy, distributed documents makes finding relevant answers difficult, especially when the answer requires connecting evidence from multiple sources. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often struggle with this type of “multi-hop” reasoning and frequently face issues with context fragmentation. In this paper, we propose a hybrid RAG framework that integrates the structured reasoning of knowledge graphs with the broad semantic coverage of dense vector retrieval. Our approach employs a multi-stage pipeline using transformer-based summarization and semantic chunking to improve context retention. We construct a dynamic knowledge graph to capture explicit relationships between entities while simultaneously maintaining a dense vector index. During inference, the system uses a hierarchical mechanism that prioritizes graph traversal for precision and falls back to vector retrieval when necessary. We evaluated our framework on the MultiHop-RAG dataset. The results show that this hybrid approach outperforms standalone vector and graph-based baselines, achieving higher Exact Match scores and improved retrieval accuracy for complex queries. This confirms that merging structured reasoning with standard vector retrieval creates a more robust system for handling complex knowledge-intensive questions.

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into workflows that require reasoning over text documents, yet interaction remains largely conversational. This leaves argumentative structure implicit or embedded in text, making it difficult to maintain, compare, and revise arguments as analyses evolve. We present GroundWork, a mixed-initiative system that makes argument structure a shared, editable state for humans and LLMs. GroundWork operationalizes the Toulmin model of argumentation as a typed graph with explicit operations for human and LLM edits. It exposes this structure through coordinated corpus views and an editable workbench for constructing, comparing, testing, and tracing source-grounded arguments. We evaluate GroundWork through an expert study with four participants spanning consulting, product development, law, and immunology, and three use-case scenarios in intelligence, law, and medicine. Our findings show that GroundWork makes source-grounded arguments inspectable, comparable, and revisable as shared human-LLM state.

Abstract:Competitive programming problems pose distinctive challenges for Large Language Models, as they demand not only proficient code generation but also advanced algorithmic reasoning. This study presents a Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach specifically designed to enhance the capacity of Large Language Models to address such problems. Our approach integrates an embedding-based retrieval mechanism and a similarity search algorithm to identify analogous problems within a knowledge database, employing a dynamically adjusted threshold to mitigate retrieval noise. We conducted an evaluation using the CodeContests dataset, focusing on the test split problems that exhibit similarity to instances from the training split. The experimental framework considered three conditions: (i) problems provided solely with their original descriptions, (ii) problems supplemented with randomly selected examples from the training split, and (iii) problems augmented with similar examples retrieved through the proposed method. In addition, we incorporated a Min-K membership inference analysis to examine whether the generated code solutions were influenced by potential memorization of training data within the evaluated Large Language Models. This complementary perspective enables a deeper understanding of model behavior by distinguishing genuine generalization through retrieval from implicit recall of pretraining samples. Performance was assessed using both pass rates and the CodeForces Elo rating of the problems. The results provide empirical evidence that similarity-based retrieval substantially enhances Large Language Models performance in competitive programming scenarios, offering an scalable framework for improving code generation in algorithmic problem-solving contexts.

Abstract:AI agents can execute multi-step tasks on users’ behalf, yet the boundaries of acceptable delegation remain unclear. We report a scenario-based survey of 289 U.S. adults with prior AI experience covering 45 use cases across nine life domains. Each respondent evaluated one scenario per domain, producing repeated measures of automation preference, trust, collaboration, AI leadership, privacy concern, and willingness to pay. Automation preferences varied substantially across domains. Generalized estimating equation models showed that greater trust in the AI agent, desired AI leadership, prior task-specific AI use, and anticipated financial savings were associated with greater automation preference. In contrast, concerns that automation would reduce personal fulfillment predicted lower automation preference. Open-ended responses further revealed a preference for bounded autonomy, with participants often favoring substantial AI execution while retaining human involvement, oversight, or final authority. We argue that delegation is best understood as a configuration of execution, collaboration, leadership, and authority.

Abstract:The rapid improvement of generative AI (GenAI) not only increased the efficiency of practice but also empowered individuals with capabilities to explore new domains. We use an autoethnography to understand identity formation in the context of solo game development as a bioinformatics educator. With the goal of developing a create-your-own-adventure (CYOA) game, we collected data for 73 days through journal entries, interacting with communities of practices. The autoethnographer had continuously reassessed the situation, and closely interacted with communities of practice. Their prior knowledge was used to provide in-game context and to uniquely interpret game development processes. Abstract:Agentic programming can automate software-defined radio (SDR) development, but decisions can propagate from software to hardware without sufficient user visibility or control. We present DeepRadio, a human-agent workspace embedded in GNU Radio Companion (GRC) for jointly constructing, verifying, and operating physical radio systems. DeepRadio uses a dynamic and state-driven workflow to coordinate a traceable radio specification, claim-oriented cross-layer verification, and mixed-initiative control. Abstract:Fairness analyses of algorithmic decision systems typically treat the feature representation of individuals as an a priori fixed input. How well a feature representation captures what is actually decision-relevant for different people and their unique backgrounds, however, is typically left unexamined. We address this gap by modeling feature engineering as a stochastic selection process over the pooled characteristics as candidate features for a finite training population. Based on this model, we develop a new framework for uniqueness-aware feature engineering which operates in two layers. The first layer measures population heterogeneity using a multivariate hypergeometric model of feature prevalence. It shows how well an individual is represented by any given input representation and which individual of the population is “least represented” compared to their personal, reference characteristics. The second layer acts on this assessment using set-similarity measures to search for an optimum between representational fit of the population and predictive accuracy. Without assuming prior knowledge about unseen individuals, our framework grants represented humans agency over what counts as decision-relevant in their case, gives deploying institutions accountability through a publishable representation fit report, and provides each person subject to a decision transparency about their personal representation fit. We operationalize our framework as a six-step pipeline and show a proof-of-principle using synthetic data. Our approach offers a blueprint for making algorithmic decision systems accountable for how well they represent individuals during development and in production.

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) are now widely used in software development, and LLM-based coding agents are given increasing autonomy. With coding agents, many design decisions are made in the conversation between the developer and the agent. Typically, the developer starts a conversation with an agent and states their intent, the agent proposes options if needed, and the developer plans the change accordingly. Then, the resulting code is committed. However, in such scenarios, the decisions and the intent behind the changes remain in the conversation, with no link to the code they produced. In this paper, we present Tracybot, an open-source tool that integrates with VS Code, Git, and coding agents to keep track of relevant conversations in an LLM-assisted development process. Tracybot captures each change as a Tasklet which consists of optional planning prompts used to plan a change, together with a build prompt that produces it. Tracybot has two main features: (i) it maps line-level code changes made by coding agents to the Tasklets that produced them, and (ii) it allows the developer to export a Tasklet as a decision record when needed, for example when the decision concerns the architecture of the project. We developed the tool over two iterations of a design science study, while focusing the evaluation on the usability and user-friendliness of the tool. In a focus group (7 participants) and a survey (24 participants), we found that Tracybot was perceived as useful for activities like code review, and most participants found our Tasklet design and presentation to be a clear way to represent the developer’s intent. Abstract:Wearable sensors, including those embedded in VR headsets, can provide LLM-based chatbots with physiological signals that users do not explicitly communicate. We tested whether such hidden input changes persuasion. In a 2\times2 within-subjects study ( N=24 ), a chatbot argued against participants’ self-selected opinions with or without turn-level heart-rate and pupil-diameter features; sensing was disclosed halfway through the study. Before disclosure, sensing increased perceived persuasiveness by 1.42 points. Abstract:Humans increasingly use generative AI (GenAI) for decision-making assistance, yet tend to engage in such situations using quick, intuitive (System 1) rather than deliberate, analytical assessment (System 2) as reflected in Dual Process Theory. Such engagement reduces the effectiveness of human-GenAI interactions and increases associated risks. Our research investigates how to design human-GenAI interactions that promote the transition from System 1 to System 2 thinking in decision-making. Based on the Three-Stage-Model, which suggests humans switch to System 2 when conflicts are detected, we conducted an experiment (n=130) testing sequential human-GenAI interaction as a cognitive forcing nudge during problem-solving tasks. This approach, where humans decide first before receiving AI assistance, enables detection of conflicting decisions. Compared to non-sequential settings (concurrent or no AI assistance), results show the sequential condition significantly enhanced both decision performance and GenAI prompt utilization, providing valuable insights for designing more reflective and thus effective human-GenAI interactions.

Abstract:In the age of digital transformation, companies are increasingly relying on specialized software to manage the complexity of projects. However, when selecting tools, features and costs often take precedence over user experience (UX), leading to low adoption rates, user frustration, and project delays. This study empirically evaluates the user experience of leading project management tools (Jira, Trello, this http URL, Asana, and Microsoft Project) across various project scales using a mixed methods approach. The System Usability Scale (SUS) was used as the primary quantitative instrument, with data collected from 141 experienced professionals via online questionnaires. The results reveal a significant trade-off between functionality and usability. Trello achieved the highest SUS score (77.5), indicating a superior user experience for small projects and agile teams, while Microsoft Project scored the lowest (51.2), suggesting significant usability challenges despite its robust features. Jira demonstrated a balanced profile, offering powerful features with manageable complexity. Statistical analyses confirmed that the choice of the optimal tool is highly context dependent, with team size and project complexity influencing UX outcomes. The findings underscore that UX is not a secondary feature but a critical success factor for software acceptance and project effectiveness. This study provides an evidence-based framework for aligning tool selection with the project context, offers practitioners actionable insights, and identifies design opportunities for software developers.

Abstract:Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in high-risks decision-making systems across domains such as healthcare, finance, and the judicial system. As reliance on predictive models grows, so does the demand for Explainable AI (XAI) to ensure transparency, trust, and interpretability. However, existing XAI approaches often fail to present explanations in a format accessible to domain experts, limiting their practical utility. Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a bridge between complex models and end-users, offering natural language explanations. Yet, their use introduces new risks, including hallucinated outputs and lack of source traceability. To address these challenges, we propose a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) that not only combines standard predictive models with XAI techniques but also incorporates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation module as an interactive enhancer. This module grounds explanations in verified medical knowledge, reformulates technical outputs into a human-like format, and enables users-such as clinicians-to actively query the system. By fostering an interactive, human-in-the-loop environment, our approach empowers domain experts to explore model decisions, contextualize explanations, and build trust in AI-assisted diagnostics. Our contributions are (1) a 3D recognition of five shadow-boxing moves (guard, punch, slip, squat, jump), each defined by one metric measure in a body frame aligned with gravity and one threshold with hysteresis, personalised during a tutorial; (2) a rhythm stage whose discrete cues are placed on the song’s kick drum and judged on the movement’s capture time, with a delay learned for each player; and (3) a phone-only architecture, running at 30 frames per second, that turns a phone and an HDMI cable into an exergame console.

Abstract:Hand-object interactions (HOIs) can be captured by smartglasses to learn how people manipulate objects in daily life. We present EventHOI, an event-driven sensing and compression system that couples selective RGB capture with HOI-aware encoding to enable egocentric logging over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) while preserving downstream HOI logging performance. Our key insight is to use low-power event sensing both to determine when RGB capture is needed and to identify where visual detail must be preserved. A lightweight IMU-based egomotion cancellation pipeline suppresses egomotion-induced events so that residual HOI motion can guide RGB triggering and spatial compression. Compared to RGB-only baselines, EventHOI reduces always-on backend power consumption by 5.8-10.4x and uplink bandwidth by 2.9x, with minimal HOI recognition accuracy loss. Abstract:As large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate everyday stories, their portrayals can shape expectations about aging. Prior work has largely examined age stereotypes in short responses, leaving unanswered whose lives models default to imagining and how age shapes characters’ roles in complete narratives. We analyze 594 stories generated by Gemini, GPT, and Llama using text embeddings, LLM-assisted coding, and qualitative analysis. When age was unspecified, stories typically featured younger adults, with middle-aged protagonists largely absent. Older adults were often portrayed through loss, familiar routines, and help from younger characters. Even positive stories sometimes treated older adults’ achievements as surprising or portrayed others making decisions on their behalf. We suggest evaluating not only the tone of generated stories, but also who appears, what opportunities they receive, and who makes decisions. Involving older adults in these evaluations can guide writing tools toward more varied, less stereotyped portrayals of later life.

Abstract:Ask an image model for your portrait and a finished picture arrives: no first line, no second thoughts, no record of how it got there, and a different picture if you ask again. I built a portrait studio that works the other way. A sitter chooses one of eight fictional artists, each written with a city, a medium and a tempo of its own, holds still for 8 to 12 seconds, and watches a drawing of themselves appear over 44 seconds. One still is sent after consent, a hosted image model returns a private study the sitter never sees, and a compiler turns that study into one drawing document. The live drawing, the saved sheet, the vector export and the film all read that document, and a replay makes no model call, so the drawing you watch is the portrait you keep. I describe the compiler in enough detail to rebuild it and say plainly what it is: an authored reconstruction at a compressed speed, not a recorded hand. On 16 generated test studies a sheet holds 8,784 to 16,378 timed contacts, about three quarters of them fixed-grid fills and nearly all shorter than one video frame, and recompiling one study gave byte-identical output four times on one machine. The paper also traces a bug that matters more than any of that. The earlier compiler estimated the paper colour tile by tile, read dark skin as paper, and in all eight hands kept less of a deep-complexioned face than a fair one (13 to 48 percent against 41 to 56). On 80 generated studies the rebuilt engine keeps the complexion difference the study already has (raw retention 89 to 120 percent), so the fairness question has moved upstream, to the study and the hosted model. The two test sitters are generated and differ in more than complexion, and no real-face or perceptual study exists yet. The studio is live at this https URL.

Abstract:A growing literature examines the impact of engaging with AI chatbots on our relationality: our ability to form relationships with others, maintain them through life’s changes, and exit when needed. Currently, substantial work focuses on purpose-built AI companions (e.g. Replika, this http URL), with less work investigating socioemotional uses of the more widely-used general-purpose chatbots. In this paper, we present a 100-person investigation into how people engage general-purpose AI for socioemotional needs. Participants’ AI uses varied, from practicing specific social skills to seeking additional bandwidth and information as they navigated their social contexts. To explain this heterogeneity, we provide 8 states that describe how AI expands or contracts relationality for people with different levels of skills, bandwidth, and information. We then present a unified conceptual model for the role of technology in mediating human relationality, the Relational Capacity Framework, and outline future research designing appropriate roles for AI in human connection.

[HC-16] Bidirectional Modeling of mmWave Human Signals for Enhancement Synthesis

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08870
作者: Shuntian Zheng,Hoang Hai Pham,Jiaqi Li,Xiaoman Lu,Shuai He,Yu Guan
类目: Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Millimeter-wave (mmWave) is attractive for human-centered robotics in smoke, darkness, and privacy-sensitive indoor spaces: it measures reflections rather than visually identifiable imagery and remains usable without light. Deployed systems, however, face two complementary needs that run in opposite directions. Enhancement starts from a raw range-angle-Doppler (RAD) heatmap, where human returns coexist with nonhuman structure, and aims to isolate the human signal by removing nonhuman returns, yielding a clean RAD input for downstream perception. Synthesis starts from denser human geometry and aims to synthesize natural RAD observations, including environmental and hardware features, thereby expanding scarce supervision data. Although the two tasks reverse direction, both require modeling how human and nonhuman reflections coexist in the same measurement. Among RAD axes, Doppler provides motion information native to the modality, with the potential to support this modeling. We therefore cast both tasks on the dual-domain RAD heatmap and propose HeatWave, which injects Doppler when it is locally reliable, and routes Doppler asymmetrically for enhancement and synthesis within one shared backbone. This design improves both tasks: enhanced observations reduce mean per-joint position error by 11.4% relative to the raw recording, and synthesized samples that replace half of the real radar labels recover most of the activity accuracy lost to the reduced budget. Relative to an unspecialized dual-task heatmap baseline, the enhancement improves motion-critical samples under metallic clutter by 2.3times more than when geometry already suffices, and synthesis follows the same ordering with a narrower spread, providing the community with a research direction more closely aligned with the signal’s characteristics.

[HC-17] What Limits mmWave Human-State Sensing for Robot Perception?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08863
作者: Shuntian Zheng,Guangming Wang,Hongyang He,Shuai He,Yu Guan
类目: Robotics (cs.RO); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Assistive robots and search-and-rescue platforms require reliable human state sensing in smoke, darkness, and privacy-sensitive environments, where cameras and LiDAR may be unreliable Millimeter-wave radar offers an alternative that works without ambient light, penetrates smoke, and does not capture visual appearance. However, the compact arrays that fit robot size, power, and cost budgets have limited apertures, producing joint-localization errors on the order of decimeters at a few meters, large enough to compromise the safety margins and tracking accuracy a robot depends on. Existing pipelines reduce pose error through frame fusion, multiple viewpoints, return selection, or stronger estimators, but examine one technique at a time, without relating its effect to a shared measurement limit or separating gains from added information from gains from estimator completion. We address this gap with a framework that models the human and environment as one time-varying scattering field and states a Cramer-Rao type error floor for joint localization as a function of bandwidth, aperture, signal-to-noise ratio, fused frame count, phase coherence, and visibility of retained returns. We then use existing frame fusion, multi viewpoint, return selection, and pose estimation methods as matched probes of this floor rather than as competing pipelines. Under the evaluated conditions, experiments on three datasets and a live deployment show these strategies move joint localization error in the predicted directions, for example lowering mean per-joint position error from about 97 to 65 mm with a second viewpoint, while a stronger estimator mainly lowers overall error by completing joints the measurement cannot resolve. These results give the robotics community a principled basis for deciding whether to prioritize observation design or estimator capacity when deploying reliable mmWave human sensing.

Abstract:While there is an abundance of research into large language model (LLM) biases against LGBTQ+ communities, far less research has examined how and why LGBTQ+ people choose to make use of AI chatbots. In this work, we examine how LGBTQ+ people choose (not) to use AI chatbots across three domains in which LGBTQ+ users have unique needs: relationship support, mental health support, and gender or sexual health support. We surveyed 73 people (60 LGBTQ+; 13 non-LGBTQ+) on how they interact with AI chatbots and find that participants’ access to external resources, privacy concerns, and perceptions of chatbot capabilities shape whether and how they choose to make use of AI chatbots. For instance, some LGBTQ+ participants felt that chatbots might actually be less biased against LGBTQ+ people than the people they know offline. We also find that LGBTQ+ participants report using AI chatbots less frequently than non-LGBTQ+ participants across 15 specific personal health and relationship advice scenarios, citing concerns about AI sycophancy and adverse cognitive side-effects. Recognizing AI chatbots as vital (albeit imperfect) resources for LGBTQ+ people, we recommend researchers consider systemic issues that drive users to AI chatbots and design technologies (AI or otherwise) that prioritize privacy, anonymity, and real human connection.
